title: Shackle a trailer's towing lug and screw the pin fully home
instruction: Shackle the trailer's towing lug: the lug between the shackle's ears and the pin screwed fully home.
context: Coupling a trailer, cart or skip to the vehicle that will tow it is routine for industrial truck and tractor operators (O*NET 53-7051, about 800,000 US workers) and for riggers. A screw-pin shackle pinned through the drawbar's towing lug is the attachment point: the tow strap or chain is looped over the shackle's bow, and the pull goes through the bow, the pin and the lug. The pin holds the trailer only if it is screwed fully home, collar seated on the ear; a pin that is not seated can work loose. One hand holds the loose shackle's ears square around the lug while the other passes the 5/8 in pin through three holes with under 1 mm of play and screws it in, regripping between half turns. The instruction states only the goal.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y left, z up). Arms start in the ready pose. Trailer (fixed): blue steel deck 42 x 34 cm, 2 cm thick, underside 10 cm above the table, 5 cm side and back rails, from x 40 to 82, centred at y -8, on one axle at x 61 with two 18 cm rubber wheels 4 cm wide outside the deck; a riser joins it to the drawbar. Drawbar block: painted steel, 8 x 8 cm, 7.75 cm tall, from x 32 to 40, y -12 to -4, with the towing lug welded to its front face: a 15 mm steel plate 40 mm wide projecting 5 cm toward the arms, its top flush with the block's top (centre 7 cm up), a 19 mm round hole centred at x 29, y -8. Shackle: Crosby G-209 1/2 in screw pin anchor shackle (stock no. 1018455, WLL 2 t, galvanised), without its pin: 12.7 mm bow, ears 30.2 mm round and 12.7 mm thick, 20.6 mm apart, 47.8 mm inside length; upper ear a plain hole, lower ear threaded 5/8-11 UNC. It stands upright, threaded ear down, bow toward the arms, in a slotted pine stand (10 mm base) at x 27, y 7. Pin: its red steel screw pin, 5/8 in x 46 mm under a 25 mm collar, flat eye 26 x 8 mm on top, chamfered end; standing eye up in a hole in a pine block 4 x 4 x 3 cm at x 22, y -23. Nothing else on the table.
scoring: From the video, a 1 mm feeler gauge and a look at the pin. 0 if the shackle or the pin fell off the table, or the pin is not through the upper ear, the lug and into the lower ear (tilted under 10 degrees). Otherwise: 1.0 if the pin is fully seated: its collar within 1 mm of the upper ear (the gauge does not fit between them; success, held 1 s); 0.5 if the pin is threaded at least one full turn but not seated; 0.25 if the pin is through all three but not threaded. The thread pulls the pin down 2.31 mm per clockwise turn, so the collar only seats once the pin has been screwed home; pressing it down does not seat it.
reset_notes: Unscrew the pin, take the shackle off the lug, stand the shackle upright in its slotted stand (threaded ear down, bow toward the arms) and the pin eye up in its holder; both stands in their taped outlines. The trailer does not move.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes (round parts as 16-sided prisms). The thread is emulated: once the pin's end rests centred on the lower ear, a joint lets it turn and slide, its height following the real 2.31 mm pitch, 0.05 N m running friction. The engaged thread is shortened to 2.5 turns (real ear: about 5.5) to fit the 1-minute run. Trailer, block and lug fixed. Details in README.
